dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality. To help me understand your back pain, have you noticed any weakness in your leg or any changes in your bowel or bladder control?
No, I haven't noticed any weakness in my leg, and my bowel and bladder function seem completely normal. It's really just this sharp pain that shoots down from my lower back all the way to my foot.
I understand. Are you experiencing any numbness or tingling in your leg or foot, and does the pain feel worse when you sit, cough, or sneeze? REQUEST TEST: Straight_Leg_Raise_Test.
RESULTS: Positive straight leg raise test with pain radiating down the leg.
The positive straight leg raise test suggests some nerve irritation. Do you feel any numbness or tingling in your foot, and did this pain start after you lifted something heavy?
Yes, there's definitely some tingling in my foot, especially on the outer side. And I was doing deadlifts at the gym when it happened - I felt that sharp pain right in the middle of a lift.

I see; the tingling on the outer side of your foot often points to a specific nerve root in your lower back being affected. Could you try standing on your toes and then your heels to see if you have any difficulty supporting your weight?

REQUEST TEST: Achilles_Reflex
RESULTS: Normal ankle and knee reflexes.

It's good that your reflexes are normal. Were you able to stand on your toes and heels without any trouble, or did you notice any weakness?
